analysis/pyproject.toml.content: The glob `tests/*.py` only matches test modules directly under `tests/`. Nested test files exist (e.g. `tests/owner/test_owner_library.py`, `tests/validation/test_validation_set.py`) and they use bare `assert` (S101), module-level imports after code (E402), unused args (ARG), etc. Under the strict selected rule set (`S`, `ARG`, `E`, ...) `ruff check` will FAIL on those nested files because the relaxations never apply. Add a recursive pattern.

`PLR2004` is silenced for tests below, but the `PLR` family is not part of `select`, so this ignore is dead code (silently ineffective). Either add `PLR` to the selected rules or drop `PLR2004` from the per-file-ignores to avoid misleading configuration.

`extraPaths` omits `src`, yet this is a src-layout project (`analysis/src/autolight_analysis/`). Unless the package happens to be installed in the analyzed environment, Pyright cannot resolve `import autolight_analysis...` (used by tests and by the package's own modules), so those imports degrade to untyped `Any` and real type errors in production code paths are masked. Add `src` to `extraPaths` (or configure `venvPath`/`venv`).

For a src-layout package, tests can only do `import autolight_analysis...` if the project is installed first; `conftest.py` only adds `tests/` and `tests/fixtures` to `sys.path`, not `src/`. A plain `pytest` run in a fresh checkout (no editable install) will fail with `ModuleNotFoundError`. Add `pythonpath = ["src"]` so collection works without a prior install.

`pydantic>=2.13.5` pins a very specific patch-level minimum. If that exact version does not exist on the index, `pip install` of the project fails outright (hard install error, not a resolution fallback). Please confirm the version exists and prefer a released, verified floor (e.g. `>=2.13` or the actual latest published patch).

apps/desktop/electron/services/simulator.content: `await show.start()` is invoked *before* the `try` block in every streaming test (this one, the snapshot test, and the B/A test). If `start()` throws or only partially completes, the `finally { await show.shutdown(); }` is never reached, so the UDP socket / timer / reader loop started by `start()` is leaked into the next test and the suite can hang or cross-contaminate. Move `start()` inside the guarded region so cleanup always runs.

The stream is synchronized with a bare `setTimeout` fixed delay. This is inherently flaky: under CI load 300ms may not be enough for a razer frame to be produced, making `frames.length > 0` and the `varied` assertion fail nondeterministically (and, conversely, pass by luck). Prefer polling/waiting for an observable produced frame (e.g. a helper that retries until `show.frames().length > 0` with a bounded timeout) rather than a fixed sleep.

await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 300));
      const frames = show.frames();

There is also no assertion that a frame actually exists. Assert the frame presence explicitly before checking its contents.

apps/desktop/scripts/run-rkbx-link.mjs.content: The header contract states step 3 "Prints the sudo command the owner pastes into a terminal", but `sudoCmd` is referenced only inside the `if (dryRun)` branch. On a normal run the owner never sees the command they are supposed to run, so the script never fulfils its primary purpose — and the 10s listener (step 4) starts before the command is even known. Print the command on the normal path as well.

`startsWith` treats each known offsets version as a prefix of the in-use version, so a known `7.2.1` wrongly matches query `7.2.19` and suppresses the honest "no offsets" warning (false negative). Compare exact versions instead.

`done()` is wired to both the socket `error` handler and the 10s timer. On a bind failure (e.g. EADDRINUSE) `error` can fire before the socket is running, and `socket.close()` on a socket with no handle throws ERR_SOCKET_DGRAM_NOT_RUNNING, masking the real error before the FAILURE line prints. Guard the close, clear the pending timer, and report a bind failure distinctly from a genuinely quiet sidecar (which is when the "check sudo prompt..." text is actually appropriate).

`readFileSync` runs unguarded immediately after `existsSync` (TOCTOU), so a permission error or a file that disappears between the two calls throws an uncaught stack instead of the script's own `fail()` message. It also executes before the `--dry-run` exit, contradicting the header's "--dry-run ... without touching ... disk" contract.

Hardcoded default Rekordbox version `7.2.19` is a business value that will silently rot as Rekordbox updates; when the env var is unset the script reports on a version nobody is actually running. Require an explicit version (fail clearly) or otherwise derive it.
The "as of 2026-10-12" claim is hardcoded and will become misleading over time. Derive the date (e.g. from the offsets file mtime) or drop it from the message.
apps/desktop/scripts/run-rkbx-link.mjs.existing_code: console.log(`no ${rekordboxVersion} offsets upstream as of 2026-10-12: sidecar will start but likely sends no packets.`);

apps/desktop/scripts/run-rkbx-link.mjs.content: Paths are interpolated into a shell command inside double quotes without escaping. A homedir containing `"`, a backtick, `$(...)` or other shell metacharacters produces a broken — or injected — command for the owner to paste. Shell-quote/escape the paths before building the command.

apps/desktop/src/routes/live/manual-inte.content:
`intent.channel in channels` walks the prototype chain and only tests key existence, so a bogus/non-implemented name that happens to be inherited (e.g. `"toString"`, `"constructor"`, `"valueOf"`) would still make this assertion pass. The test name claims to verify "only implemented typed channels" but does not. Use an own-property check and, ideally, validate the payload against the channel's request schema so a channel/payload mismatch is also caught. E.g.:
```ts
expect(Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(channels, intent.channel)).toBe(true);
```

These `toMatchObject` assertions only inspect a subset of keys, so they cannot detect a wrong/missing intent channel or extra payload fields. Notably `blinderIntent(64)` is asserted solely on `payload.at` while its channel is actually `"show/trigger-build"` (and that channel's request schema is `z.object({ version: v1 })`, which has no `at`); a mis-wired channel or a stripped/unexpected payload field would go unnoticed. `palettePickIntent` is only checked for `custom` and `flashIntent` only for `channel`. Assert the full intent (`channel` + `payload`) for each helper, and for helpers bound to a channel validate the payload with that channel's request schema.

This assertion pins the clamp result at `2` for input `9`, but the `master/intensity` request schema in `@autolight/ipc` is `z.object({ version: v1, value: z.number().min(0).max(1) })` — a value of `2` is outside the contract and would be rejected at runtime. `manual-intents.ts` clamps with `Math.min(2, Math.max(0.5, value))`, so the test locks in a contract-violating bound instead of catching it. Assert a value within `[0, 1]` (and add negative/NaN/lower-bound cases) so the mismatch surfaces.

The fabricated `as unknown as TrackModel` fixture is never validated against the real model, and `toHaveLength(2)` only counts entries — it does not verify the returned colours, so an incorrect `SWATCH_BY_KIND` mapping (or falling back to the white default) would still pass. Also, because the two kinds are distinct this never exercises the de-duplication logic the description implies. Assert the actual swatch values and include a repeated `kind` to cover dedup.

Additionally, when the document is a non-object (e.g. `42`, `true`, `"x"`) or carries an unexpected `version`, `Object.entries` yields nothing and the method silently returns `ok: true` while importing no values. This diverges from `validateImportValues` in store.ts, which parses `def.range` and rejects out-of-bounds / NaN values — a round trip through this method bypasses that enforcement. Either extract/reuse `validateImportValues` or add the range and `Number.isNaN` checks here.

`layerOf` keys off `Map.has()`, but `get()` treats an explicit `undefined` as "absent" (`v !== undefined`) and falls through to the default. After `set(scope, key, undefined)` the two disagree: `layerOf(key)` returns the scope while `get(key)` returns the built-in default. `changedOnly()` then emits an inconsistent `{ value: <default>, layer: <scope> }`, i.e. it reports a "changed" entry whose value equals the default. Use the same presence semantics in both methods (`has()` in `get`, or document that `undefined` is not a storable value and reject it in `set`).

`exportJson` flattens every key to its effective value, including built-in defaults, and drops which layer produced it. `importJson` then re-inserts all of them into the `app` layer, so an export/import round trip silently promotes built-in defaults into explicit app-layer overrides and loses the original origin layer (session/device/style). Combined with `importJson` never clearing the other layers, importing an exported document does not reproduce the exported state. Persist per-layer values (as `readLayersFile` does via `layers`) or document/handle the flattening explicitly.
